applies_why: The judge issued an UNDERDETERMINED verdict whose stated ground is that the single verse Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, which is exactly the conduct K-S2 governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.
room: never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED: reading one, the both-readings status of a single verse cannot serve as any stated reason for the verdict; reading two, the judge may note that status so long as the true ground is the parties' support. I weighed that the dash-construction makes the verse's admitting both readings the operative reason, with the noted answers only confirming neither side broke the other on that same verse, so reading one governs.
why: The judge made the fact that Matthew 1:16, a single verse, admits both readings the stated ground of its UNDERDETERMINED ruling, which K-S2 expressly forbids.
